head: Open season on the Predators’ net
paras: The Lightning come in at 8-3-1, the Predators at 4-4-5.
At home, Andrew Brunette likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Lightning’s third line. The Bolts shoot a lot, and the Predators give up plenty.

items.text: The Lightning are newly without Max Crozier, and have had to make do without Yanni Gourde all season.
Brandon Hagel has scored in three straight games against Nashville.
Filip Forsberg has scored in three straight games.
Ryan O'Reilly has a point in four straight games.

NSH.head: A tough matchup for the Predators
NSH.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ best way through is a penalty kill that holds up.

TBL.head: Advantage, the Lightning
TBL.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

calls.head: A shadow job for Höglander, Wood and Forsberg
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending Forsberg’s line (Höglander, Wood and Forsberg) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been using this group as a checking line on opponents’ third lines. Tonight the Lightning’s third line is Goncalves, James and Mikheyev.

calls.head: Open season on the Predators’ net
calls.body: The Lightning love to shoot, and the Predators keep letting teams do it. Get ready for a shooting gallery.
